title: Spread of Buddhism across Asia
summary: Taxila, in present-day Pakistan, was an important Buddhist centre of learning from the 5th century BCE to the 2nd century CE. During the 2nd century CE, Buddhism began to spread vigorously into Central Asia and China with the active support of local rulers. The Mogao Caves, at a strategic point on the Silk Route, record its religious and cultural influence.

uncertainty.note: Start reflects the 3rd century BCE expansion under Mauryan patronage and Gandharan contact; transmission continued actively along Silk Road and maritime networks through the 6th century CE across East and Southeast Asia.

importance.justification: The transcontinental transmission of Buddhism connected South, Central, and East Asia, fostering deep cultural, philosophical, and artistic synthesis across Eurasia.

related.because: The foundational emergence of Buddhism in northern India provided the doctrine and monastic order that later expanded across Asia.
